review_notes: I read the file's definitions and checked those that look like Mathlib concepts: pairing, supportFunction, normalizedVolume, barycenter, standardSimplex, dualVector, and the upper-regularization and Legendre-transform definitions. I did not check every proof body or every use site. Findings: `pairing` duplicates `dotProduct`, `normalizedVolume` duplicates `Measure.real`, and `barycenter` duplicates the set average `⨍`. Not reported: `standardSimplex` (Mathlib's `stdSimplex` requires the sum to equal 1, so it is a different set), and `supportFunction` and `legendreTransform` (a grep of Mathlib found no support-function definition and no Legendre-transform definition). The dotProduct and Measure.real matches rest on Mathlib's definitions, which I did not re-read in full. I did not check how many of the pairing lemmas are only used internally. No Lean was run.

findings.declaration: Ehrhart.SupportFunction.pairing (and the lemmas pairing_add_left, pairing_smul_left, pairing_sub_left, pairing_add_right, pairing_smul_right, pairing_sub_right)
findings.excerpt:
private def pairing {n : ℕ} (u x : Space n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, u i * x i
findings.problem: `pairing u x = ∑ i, u i * x i` on `Fin n → ℝ` is exactly Mathlib's `dotProduct` (`u ⬝ᵥ x`). The file re-proves linearity facts that Mathlib already has, as six separate lemmas. These are `pairing_add_left` (line 321), `pairing_smul_left` (326), `pairing_sub_left` (612), `pairing_add_right` (619), `pairing_smul_right` (626) and `pairing_sub_right` (1695). It also builds `pairingLinear` (line 2314) by hand for `map_add'` and `map_smul'`, and uses `mul_comm` unfoldings to swap arguments (`pairing_actualGradient_eq_fderiv`, `sourcePairingContinuousLinear_apply`). Continuity (`continuous_pairing_left/right`) is also redone from scratch.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the private `pairing` and use `u ⬝ᵥ x` directly. If the name is wanted, keep `pairing` as an `abbrev` for `dotProduct`. Replace the six linearity lemmas with Mathlib's `add_dotProduct`, `dotProduct_add`, `smul_dotProduct`, `dotProduct_smul`, `sub_dotProduct`, `dotProduct_sub` and `dotProduct_comm`. Build `pairingLinear` from `Matrix.dotProductBilin` or `Matrix.toLin'`. Obtain continuity from `fun_prop`/`continuous_finsetSum` once, on `dotProduct`.
findings.benefit: Removes about six near-identical private lemmas and several manual `simp only` unfoldings. Readers get standard notation and simp lemmas, and the pairing integrates with the rest of Mathlib's linear algebra instead of being a private island.

findings.excerpt:
def normalizedVolume {n : ℕ} (K : Set (Space n)) : ℝ :=
  ((volume : Measure (Space n)) K).toReal
findings.problem: `normalizedVolume K` is by definition `(volume K).toReal`, which is `Measure.real volume K`. Mathlib already has `Measure.real` with the `measureReal_*` API (`measureReal_def`, `measureReal_restrict_apply`, `measureReal_univ`, ...). The file keeps two parallel notions. Some proofs use `volume.real` (`real_volume_ball_inv_nat`, `realVolume_uniformInnerBall`, `normalizedVolume_standardSimplex`), while others use `normalizedVolume`. Conversions are needed repeatedly, for example `unfold Measure.real normalizedVolume`, `simp only [... measureReal_def, ..., normalizedVolume]`, and `simpa only [ne_eq, normalizedVolume] using K.volume_pos.ne'`. Despite the name, nothing is normalized, so the name is also misleading.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `normalizedVolume K` by `(volume : Measure (Space n)).real K` throughout. If a short name is wanted, make it `abbrev normalizedVolume K := (volume : Measure (Space n)).real K` so the `measureReal_*` lemmas apply without unfolding. The `normalizedVolume`-specific conversions then disappear.
findings.benefit: Avoids a second real-valued volume notion that needs unfolding or bridging lemmas. Mathlib's measureReal simp lemmas (restrict, union, smul, ...) apply directly, and the repeated `unfold normalizedVolume`/`measureReal_def` steps become unnecessary.

findings.excerpt:
def barycenter {n : ℕ} (K : Set (Space n)) : Space n :=
  (normalizedVolume K)⁻¹ • ∫ x in K, x ∂(volume : Measure (Space n))
findings.problem: `barycenter K` is the average of the identity on `K` w.r.t. Lebesgue measure. That is Mathlib's set average `⨍ x in K, x`, defined via `average` and unfolded by `average_eq` to `(μ.real univ)⁻¹ • ∫ x, f x ∂μ`, applied to `volume.restrict K`. The file reimplements it by hand and then has to manually extract the integral from the `centered` hypothesis: `sourceCenteredBody_setIntegral_id_eq_zero` uses `simpa only [smul_eq_zero, inv_eq_zero, barycenter] using K.centered` and then `resolve_left` with a volume-positivity argument.
findings.proposed_change: Define `barycenter K := ⨍ x in K, x ∂(volume : Measure (Space n))` (or state `CenteredBody.centered` with `⨍`) and use `average_eq` and the `setAverage` API. Keep the name `barycenter` as a thin alias if desired.
findings.benefit: Uses the standard averaging notion and its lemma library (`average_eq`, `setAverage_eq`, ...) instead of a one-off normalization, and removes the duplicated `smul_eq_zero` plumbing. This also removes the dependence on the nonstandard `normalizedVolume`.
